learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Exploration progress is not mastery evidence; quiz attempts remain the scored retrieval signal.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Identity + action + resource + conditions → authorization __________.

reveal.text: AWS evaluates applicable policies and context to determine whether a request is allowed.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Explicit deny beats __________.

reveal.text: An applicable explicit deny overrides allows.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Authentication = who are you; authorization = what may you __________.

reveal.text: Keep identity verification separate from permission evaluation.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Role = permissions assumed with temporary __________.

reveal.text: Roles provide temporary credentials to trusted principals/services instead of long-lived user keys.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Trust policy = who can assume; permissions policy = what they can __________.

reveal.text: Both sides matter for role access.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: EC2 needs AWS API access without stored keys → __________.

reveal.text: Attach/associate an IAM role appropriate for the workload.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Policy attached to the __________ rather than an identity.

reveal.text: Resource-based policies specify which principals may access that resource and under what conditions.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Common with S3 buckets, KMS keys, SNS/SQS, and other supported __________.

reveal.text: Use the resource policy model when the service/resource supports it.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Identity policy and resource policy can both affect one __________.

reveal.text: Evaluate the complete policy context rather than assuming only one policy applies.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Limit a permission by request __________.

reveal.text: Condition keys restrict when a policy statement applies, based on context such as tags, source, organization, or MFA.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Require requests from organization/VPC endpoint/tag/MFA → use policy __________.

reveal.text: Conditions let you enforce contextual access rules.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: A condition does not create permission if the action is not otherwise __________.

reveal.text: It narrows when a statement applies.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: MFA adds another authentication __________.

reveal.text: MFA requires an additional factor beyond the primary credential.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Especially important for privileged interactive access and sensitive __________.

reveal.text: Protect high-impact access paths with strong authentication.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: MFA does not replace least-privilege __________.

reveal.text: Strong authentication and authorization controls are complementary.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Analyzes access paths/policies to identify unintended external/public __________.

reveal.text: Access Analyzer helps identify resource access and validate IAM policies using policy analysis.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use to find resources shared outside the intended zone of __________.

reveal.text: Define/analyze trusted access boundaries and investigate findings.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Access Analyzer ≠ CloudTrail.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Test whether policies would allow/deny selected actions without making the actual __________.

reveal.text: The policy simulator evaluates policy behavior for specified requests.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Troubleshoot “why is this identity denied?” together with __________ and CloudTrail.

reveal.text: Use simulation plus actual request context and audit history.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Simulation is not a substitute for testing all service-specific/resource-policy __________.

reveal.text: Interpret results within the complete authorization model.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Shows which principal called which AWS __________ and when.

reveal.text: CloudTrail records AWS API activity that helps investigate access and changes.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Who changed this policy?” → __________.

reveal.text: CloudTrail is the audit trail clue.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: CloudTrail does not calculate effective IAM permissions by __________.

reveal.text: Use IAM analysis tools/policy evaluation for that question.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Centrally organize AWS accounts into roots and __________.

reveal.text: Organizations groups accounts into organizational units and supports centralized governance.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use for multi-account governance, consolidated administration, and policy __________.

reveal.text: Organizations is the foundation for many multi-account controls.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: An OU is not an IAM group for human __________.

reveal.text: It groups AWS accounts, not users.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: SCP = maximum permissions boundary for member accounts; it does not grant __________.

reveal.text: Identity/resource policies still need to allow an action; SCPs limit what can be allowed.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: SCP / IAM policy

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Prevent member accounts from using service/Region even if admins allow it” → __________.

reveal.text: Use an SCP as an organization guardrail where applicable.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Central workforce access to multiple AWS accounts/applications using __________.

reveal.text: IAM Identity Center centralizes workforce identities/assignments and single sign-on access.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Many human users need managed access across many accounts → __________.

reveal.text: IAM Identity Center is a strong multi-account workforce-access pattern.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Workload service-to-service access still commonly uses IAM __________.

reveal.text: Identity Center is mainly for workforce access; workloads generally use roles.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Checks AWS environment against selected best-practice __________.

reveal.text: Trusted Advisor surfaces recommendations in areas including security, resilience, performance, cost, and service limits depending on support/features.

prompts.label: ⚡ ACTION
prompts.placeholder: Finding → validate impact → remediate configuration → __________.

reveal.text: Recheck/confirm the issue is resolved.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Trusted Advisor is not a full continuous resource-configuration history like __________.

reveal.text: AWS Config provides configuration recording/evaluation capabilities.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Records supported resource configuration and evaluates it against __________.

reveal.text: AWS Config tracks configuration state/changes and can evaluate resources using rules.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use for “was this resource compliant at time X?” or “how did configuration __________?”

reveal.text: Configuration history and compliance evaluation are core AWS Config use cases.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Config records configuration/compliance; CloudTrail records API __________.

reveal.text: Use them together to understand what changed and who initiated the change.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Bundle Config rules/remediation into a reusable compliance __________.

reveal.text: Conformance packs package a set of Config rules and remediation actions for deployment as a unit.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Apply the same compliance framework across accounts/Regions → __________.

reveal.text: Conformance packs help standardize AWS Config-based compliance.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Continuously evaluate a collection of compliance controls” → __________.

reveal.text: AWS Config rules/conformance packs.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Classify data by sensitivity/requirements before choosing __________.

reveal.text: Classification informs encryption, retention, access, monitoring, and handling controls.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Public / internal / confidential / regulated are examples of __________ tiers.

reveal.text: Use an organization-defined classification scheme tied to handling requirements.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Encryption does not remove the need for access control, retention, and __________.

reveal.text: Data protection is layered.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Managed service for creating/controlling cryptographic __________.

reveal.text: AWS KMS manages keys used by many AWS services for encryption and signing use cases.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Data key encrypts data; KMS key protects/controls the data __________.

reveal.text: Envelope encryption commonly uses data keys protected by KMS keys.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Customer-controlled encryption key, rotation, audit of key use” → __________.

reveal.text: AWS KMS is a common answer.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: KMS access can involve key policy + IAM policy + grants + __________.

reveal.text: Authorization depends on the key policy and applicable permission mechanisms/context.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: AccessDenied on encrypted resource? Check both service/resource access and KMS __________.

reveal.text: The caller/service must also be allowed to use the key for the required cryptographic operation.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Having S3/RDS permission does not automatically grant KMS __________.

reveal.text: Encryption-key permissions are a separate authorization layer.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Provision/manage TLS certificates for supported AWS __________.

reveal.text: ACM manages public/private certificates used by supported integrated services.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Need managed certificate renewal on ALB/CloudFront/etc. → __________.

reveal.text: ACM is designed to simplify certificate lifecycle for supported integrations.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: ACM protects data in transit; KMS is commonly associated with encryption at __________.

reveal.text: Use the control that matches the data-protection layer.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Store and retrieve secrets such as DB credentials/API keys with controlled __________.

reveal.text: Secrets Manager provides managed secret storage and access, with rotation features for supported patterns.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Need managed credential rotation → consider __________.

reveal.text: Secrets Manager is a direct clue when rotation is a core requirement.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Do not hard-code secrets in source code, AMIs, or plain environment __________.

reveal.text: Retrieve secrets securely at runtime with least-privilege access.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Secrets Manager / Parameter Store

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Automatic managed rotation is a strong clue for __________.

reveal.text: Secrets Manager.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Choose based on secret lifecycle, rotation, hierarchy/configuration needs, and __________.

reveal.text: Also consider integration and cost/operational requirements.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Uses managed data-security capabilities to discover sensitive data in __________.

reveal.text: Macie helps identify sensitive data and security issues in Amazon S3.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: “Find PII/sensitive data in S3” → __________.

reveal.text: Amazon Macie is the direct clue.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Macie is not a network-threat detection service like __________.

reveal.text: GuardDuty focuses on threat detection from security telemetry.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Managed threat detection using AWS security telemetry and behavioral __________.

reveal.text: GuardDuty analyzes supported logs/signals to identify suspicious or malicious activity.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Suspicious credentials, unusual API calls, malicious network behavior → __________.

reveal.text: GuardDuty is a common managed threat-detection answer.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: GuardDuty findings still require triage/remediation; it is not an automatic firewall __________.

reveal.text: Integrate findings with response workflows as appropriate.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Continuously scans supported compute/container workloads for software vulnerabilities and unintended network __________.

reveal.text: Inspector helps identify package vulnerabilities and supported exposure risks.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: “Which EC2/ECR/Lambda workloads have vulnerable packages?” → __________.

reveal.text: Amazon Inspector is the direct clue.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Inspector ≠ GuardDuty.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Aggregates/normalizes security findings and evaluates security __________.

reveal.text: Security Hub provides a centralized view of findings and security posture from supported services/integrations.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Need one place to triage findings across GuardDuty/Inspector/etc. → __________.

reveal.text: AWS Security Hub.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Security Hub aggregates/evaluates; the source service may still be the one that __________ the issue.

reveal.text: Understand where a finding originates and where remediation belongs.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Current SOA-C03 scope includes AWS Security Agent as an example in security findings/remediation __________.

reveal.text: Recognize it as a current AWS security capability included in exam-guide version 1.1.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Use findings with least-privilege, evidence, and controlled __________.

reveal.text: Security automation should remain auditable and bounded by permissions.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: If the scenario explicitly names AWS Security Agent, know it belongs to the current security/remediation __________.

reveal.text: The exam guide added it to Skill 4.2.5 in revision 1.1.

authoring_notes: Original learning content. Official SOA-C03 exam guide revision 1.1 is the scope authority; the supplied May 2026 study guide was used as a supplementary coverage check and was not copied.
